procedures.description: Open appendicectomy through a right lower quadrant incision. The bread-and-butter emergency case.
procedures.tutorial: Work down through skin, fat and muscle with the scalpel, staying on the dotted guide line. Clamp the appendix base before you divide it - dividing an unclamped structure bleeds. Then lift it out with forceps and close the skin.

patient.name: Marcus Delgado
patient.history: Previously fit and well. No prior abdominal surgery.
patient.presentation: Twelve hours of periumbilical pain migrating to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low grade fever. Rebound tenderness at McBurney's point.
patient.imagingCaption: Ultrasound shows a non-compressible, thickened appendix with surrounding fat stranding. No free fluid.

steps.title: Review the patient chart
steps.description: Confirm identity, allergies and the working diagnosis.
steps.hint: Press Tab to open the chart.

steps.title: Review the imaging
steps.description: Check the ultrasound on the wall display.
steps.hint: Walk to the imaging display and press E.

steps.title: Scrub in
steps.description: Scrub, gown and glove at the sink.
steps.hint: Press E at the scrub sink by the door.

steps.title: Prep and drape the patient
steps.description: Skin prep, drapes and induction of anaesthesia.
steps.hint: Press E at the prep zone beside the table.

steps.title: Right lower quadrant incision
steps.description: Open the skin along the marked line.
steps.hint: Hold left mouse on the dotted guide. Shift steadies your hand.

steps.title: Divide the subcutaneous fat
steps.hint: Same technique, one layer deeper.

steps.title: Open the abdominal wall
steps.description: Split the muscle layer and enter the peritoneum.
steps.hint: Careful - bowel lies immediately underneath.

steps.title: Retract the wound edges
steps.description: Hold the wall open for exposure.
steps.hint: Hold left mouse with the retractor, or order the assistant to hold it (F7).

steps.title: Identify the appendix
steps.description: Confirm the inflamed appendix before dividing anything.
steps.hint: Right click on the appendix with forceps to identify it.

steps.title: Clamp the appendix base
steps.hint: Left click on the appendix with the hemostat.

steps.title: Divide the appendix
steps.hint: Right click on the clamped appendix with the scalpel.

steps.title: Remove the appendix
steps.description: Lift the specimen clear of the abdomen.
steps.hint: Left click on the divided appendix with forceps.

steps.title: Check for bleeding
steps.description: Clear the field and confirm haemostasis.
steps.hint: Hold left mouse with the suction in the open abdomen.

steps.title: Close the incision
steps.description: Approximate the skin edges with interrupted sutures.
steps.hint: Place four evenly spaced stitches along the wound.

procedures.description: Penetrating abdominal trauma with bowel injury and mesenteric bleeding. Damage control laparotomy.
procedures.tutorial: Speed matters. Open the abdomen, suction the blood so you can see, then work systematically: control the mesenteric bleeding first, repair the bowel, and only then go looking for the bullet.

patient.name: Ana Whitfield
patient.presentation: Single gunshot wound to the left upper quadrant. Hypotensive on arrival, positive FAST scan, taken directly to theatre.
patient.imagingCaption: FAST scan positive for free intraperitoneal fluid. Radio-opaque fragment projected over the left mid abdomen.

steps.title: Review the chart
steps.description: Blood type, allergies and mechanism of injury.
steps.hint: Press Tab.

steps.title: Scrub in
steps.hint: Press E at the scrub sink.

steps.title: Prep and drape
steps.description: Rapid prep - this is a damage control case.
steps.hint: Press E at the prep zone.

steps.title: Examine the entry wound
steps.hint: Right click the entry wound with forceps.

steps.title: Midline laparotomy incision
steps.description: Long midline incision for full exposure.
steps.hint: Follow the guide line.

steps.title: Enter the abdomen
steps.description: Divide the abdominal wall and enter the peritoneum.

steps.title: Suction the blood
steps.description: Clear the field so you can find the bleeding.
steps.hint: Hold left mouse in the pooled blood.

steps.title: Control the mesenteric bleeding
steps.hint: Click directly on the pulsing bleeders.

steps.title: Repair the bowel perforations
steps.hint: Place five well spaced stitches along the bowel.

steps.title: Remove the bullet
steps.description: Retrieve the projectile if it can be reached safely.
steps.hint: Look for the dark fragment among the bowel loops.

steps.title: Washout
steps.hint: Hold left mouse with the irrigation device.

procedures.description: Blunt abdominal trauma with a grade IV splenic laceration and ongoing haemorrhage.
procedures.tutorial: This patient is bleeding to death. Get in fast, pack and clamp the hilum, then decide: attempt repair, or take the spleen out. If the bleeding is not controlled within a couple of minutes, stop trying to save it.

patient.name: Tomas Novak
patient.history: Motorcycle collision at speed. Helmeted. Left flank impact.
patient.presentation: Hypotensive despite two litres of crystalloid. Left upper quadrant tenderness with Kehr's sign. Taken straight to theatre.
patient.imagingCaption: CT shows a grade IV splenic laceration with active contrast extravasation and large haemoperitoneum.

steps.title: Review the chart
steps.description: Confirm blood products are on the way.
steps.hint: Press Tab.

steps.title: Scrub in
steps.description: Fast scrub - the patient is unstable.

steps.title: Pack the left upper quadrant
steps.description: Temporary control while you get exposure.
steps.hint: Remember to take the sponge out before you close.

steps.title: Suction the haemoperitoneum
steps.description: Clear the blood to see the injury.

steps.title: Control the splenic hilum
steps.hint: Click on the bleeders on the spleen.

steps.title: Attempt splenic repair
steps.description: Try to salvage the spleen if the injury allows.
steps.hint: Optional - a grade IV laceration usually cannot be saved.

steps.title: Divide the splenic pedicle
steps.hint: Right click on the clamped spleen.

steps.title: Perform the splenectomy
steps.description: Deliver the spleen out of the abdomen.

steps.title: Stabilise the blood pressure
steps.hint: Order blood on the command wheel (F3) and give tranexamic acid or a vasopressor.

procedures.description: Traumatic pneumothorax with progressive hypoxia. Needs decompression and a chest drain.
procedures.tutorial: The patient's saturations are falling. Cut down over the rib in the safe triangle, get into the pleural space - not the lung - and confirm the tube swings and drains.

patient.name: Priya Kaur
patient.presentation: Fall from height with left sided chest wall pain, reduced air entry on the left and falling oxygen saturations despite high flow oxygen.
patient.imagingCaption: Chest radiograph shows a large left pneumothorax with early mediastinal shift.

steps.title: Assess oxygen saturation
steps.description: Check the monitor and the chart.
steps.hint: Press Tab - note the saturations.

steps.title: Review the chest film
steps.description: Confirm the side before you cut.
steps.hint: Press E at the imaging display.

steps.title: Prep and drape the chest
steps.description: Prep the left lateral chest wall.

steps.title: Divide the muscle
steps.description: Blunt dissection down to the pleura.

steps.title: Insert the chest tube
steps.description: Into the pleural space, over the rib.
steps.hint: Aim at the pleural space, never the lung itself.

steps.title: Confirm placement
steps.description: Check the tube swings and drains.
steps.hint: Right click with the chest tube.

steps.title: Reassess lung expansion
steps.hint: Right click on the lung to reassess it.

steps.title: Secure the tube
steps.description: Anchor the drain with a stitch.

procedures.description: Contaminated open midshaft femoral fracture. Washout, reduction and plate fixation.
procedures.tutorial: Irrigate before you fix - contamination left behind becomes osteomyelitis. Reduce the fracture (right click with the plate tool) before you seat the plate, drill your pilot holes, then drive the screws with the drill.

patient.name: Kwame Osei
patient.presentation: Crush injury to the left thigh with bone visible through a ten centimetre wound. Distal pulses present. Grossly contaminated.
patient.imagingCaption: Radiograph shows a comminuted midshaft femoral fracture with soft tissue gas.

steps.title: Review the chart
steps.description: Note the latex allergy and the contamination.
steps.hint: Press Tab.

steps.title: Irrigate the wound
steps.description: Copious washout of the contaminated wound.
steps.hint: Hold left mouse over the open wound.

steps.title: Control the bleeding
steps.hint: Click on each pulsing bleeder.

steps.title: Reduce and align the fracture
steps.description: Bring the bone ends back into alignment.
steps.hint: Right click on the femur with the fixation plate tool, repeatedly.

steps.title: Drill the pilot holes
steps.description: Four pilot holes spaced along the shaft.
steps.hint: Hold left mouse, then move along the bone for the next hole.

steps.title: Seat the fixation plate
steps.description: Lay the plate across the fracture.
steps.hint: Left click on the reduced femur.

steps.title: Drive the screws
steps.description: Secure the plate to the bone.
steps.hint: Right click with the drill, once per pilot hole.

procedures.description: Single vessel bypass to the left anterior descending artery via median sternotomy.
procedures.tutorial: Sternotomy first, then the spreader - trying to spread intact ribs breaks them. The anastomosis needs six accurate, well spaced stitches; sloppy stitching leaks and you will be chasing bleeding for the rest of the case.

patient.name: Dorothy Brennan
patient.history: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ex-smoker. Angiography shows a critical proximal LAD stenosis.
patient.presentation: Crescendo angina refractory to medical therapy. Booked for elective single vessel bypass grafting.
patient.imagingCaption: Coronary angiography demonstrates a 90 percent proximal LAD stenosis with good distal run-off.

steps.title: Review the chart
steps.description: Confirm the target vessel and the allergy.

steps.title: Review the angiography
steps.description: Confirm the lesion before you start.

steps.title: Median sternotomy
steps.description: Divide the sternum with the saw.
steps.hint: Steady hand - the heart is directly behind.

steps.title: Open the chest
steps.description: Place and open the rib spreader.
steps.hint: Only after the sternum is fully divided.

steps.title: Prepare the graft
steps.hint: Right click with the scalpel to prepare the graft.

steps.title: Anastomose the graft to the LAD
steps.description: Six accurate stitches around the arteriotomy.
steps.hint: Space the stitches - bunched stitches leak.

steps.title: Control the bleeding
steps.description: Seal the small bleeders around the graft.
steps.hint: Do not use cautery on the graft itself.

steps.title: Restart and stabilise the heart
steps.description: Support the myocardium as it takes over.
steps.hint: Epinephrine at the correct dose. Right click on the syringe to choose the drug.

steps.title: Internal defibrillation if required
steps.hint: Only if the rhythm is actually shockable.

steps.title: Close the chest
steps.description: Close the soft tissues over the sternum.

procedures.description: Traumatic subdural collection with midline shift. Emergency burr hole decompression.
procedures.tutorial: Read the CT and mark the correct side before you touch the scalp - a wrong-side craniotomy is a career-ending never-event. Drill gently: pressing on after the hole is through plunges the bit into the brain.

patient.name: Hiroshi Nakamura
patient.history: On low dose anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation.
patient.presentation: Fall down stairs with a lucid interval followed by a drop in conscious level. Left pupil now sluggish.
patient.imagingCaption: CT head shows a left sided acute subdural collection with 9 mm of midline shift. Operate on the LEFT.

steps.title: Review the CT imaging
steps.description: Confirm the side and the level of the collection.
steps.hint: Press E at the imaging display - the report names the side.

steps.title: Mark the correct side
steps.description: Confirm laterality on the scalp before incision.
steps.hint: Right click on the scalp to mark the side.

steps.title: Scalp incision
steps.description: Linear incision over the marked point.

steps.title: Drill the burr hole
steps.description: Through the outer and inner tables.
steps.hint: Ease off the moment you feel the bit break through.

steps.title: Evacuate the hematoma
steps.description: Remove the clot and decompress the brain.
steps.hint: Grasp the dark collection with the forceps.

steps.title: Control the bleeding
steps.hint: Small bleeders only - never on the brain surface.

procedures.description: Polytrauma: intra-abdominal bleeding, a pneumothorax and a fractured arm, all at once.
procedures.tutorial: Priorities, in order: breathing, then bleeding, then bones. Put the chest drain in before you open the abdomen, and be ready for the arrest - it is coming.

patient.name: Lena Ferreira
patient.history: No past medical history. Restrained front seat passenger.
patient.presentation: High speed road traffic collision. Hypotensive, hypoxic, with an obviously deformed left forearm and a positive FAST scan.
patient.imagingCaption: Trauma CT: left pneumothorax, liver laceration with haemoperitoneum, displaced humeral shaft fracture.

steps.title: Primary survey
steps.hint: Airway and breathing come before bleeding.

steps.title: Prep and drape
steps.description: Prep chest, abdomen and left arm.

steps.title: Incise the chest wall
steps.description: Chest drain site on the left.

steps.title: Decompress the chest
steps.description: Chest drain into the pleural space.
steps.hint: Breathing before bleeding.

steps.title: Suction the abdomen
steps.description: Clear the blood to find the source.

steps.title: Control the liver bleeding
steps.description: Clamp or pack the liver laceration.

steps.title: Manage the cardiac arrest
steps.description: If the patient arrests, start compressions.
steps.hint: Aim for 100-120 per minute. Order the assistant to take over with F4.

steps.title: Defibrillate if shockable
steps.hint: Check the rhythm on the monitor first.
